claims.text: A 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock was previously identified as optimal for HVAF-M3 deposition.
HVAF-i7 deposition with 15–45 μm feedstock and standard parameters produced acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
Increasing combustion-gas pressure and modifying the fuel-to-oxygen ratio will increase FeCoNiCrAl particle velocity and momentum.
The resulting increase in velocity will increase the particles' kinetic energy.
A stand-off distance of 300–350 mm is optimal for HVAF-i7 spraying of this alloy.
Particles with sufficient velocity form better-flattened splats.
Enhanced particle kinetic energy promotes improved interparticle bonding.
The proposed parameter changes will produce more focused particle trajectories.
Improved splat formation and interparticle bonding will increase deposition efficiency and coating thickness.
Higher particle speed combined with comparatively low particle temperature can reduce in-flight oxidation and improve coating density.
Maintaining a 300–350 mm stand-off distance provides adequate particle heating while minimizing in-flight oxidation.
The optimized HVAF-i7 process will produce a significantly thicker coating than the standard-parameter HVAF-i7 baseline.
The optimized coating will have greater adhesion than the standard-parameter baseline.
The optimized coating will retain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention will remain effective when spraying internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The thicker, more adherent, minimally oxidized coating will better meet high-temperature thermal-barrier service requirements.
Departures from the balance between particle velocity and oxidation control may compromise coating microstructure.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires increased combustion-gas pressure, whereas the conditions specify operation at standard pressures; it is unclear whether the increased pressure is within the stated standard-pressure condition.
